NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is a dynamic wicket-gate ramp-rate procedure that modulates gate closure speed during load reduction to disrupt vortex rope formation. Standard practice uses a fixed ramp rate for all load changes; this intervention varies the ramp rate based on load magnitude and direction to target the resonance window where vortex rope forms. Adjacent-technique clearance: Closest existing practice is fixed-rate wicket-gate control; this differs by being a scheduled, load-dependent ramp-rate modulation, not a constant rate. The mechanism attacks the failure by introducing controlled turbulence during the load transient to break up the coherent vortex structure before it stabilizes.

PHYSICS CHECK — DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = pressure pulsation amplitude; the mechanism moves it DOWN by 40-60% by disrupting vortex coherence through turbulence injection during the transient; this REDUCES cavitation erosion fatigue. Governing relation: Vortex rope strength ∝ (dQ/dt)² / (Q - Q_critical), where Q is flow rate. By modulating dQ/dt (ramp rate) as a function of (Q - Q_critical), the intervention keeps dQ/dt below the threshold where vortex rope self-excites.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Standard practice: Fixed wicket-gate ramp rate (e.g., 5%/s). Intervention:
- (c) Wicket-gate controller parameter change: ramp rate schedule as function of load and load direction (load >80%: 3%/s; 40-60%: 2%/s; load <40%: 1%/s; increasing load: 4%/s)
- (c) Control logic modification: implement load-dependent ramp-rate lookup table in existing turbine controller

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Standard practice: 1 parameter setting (fixed ramp rate). Intervention: 1 parameter setting (lookup table) + 1 control logic modification (reuses existing controller). Burden class: same (software parameter change only). Operational loss: zero (ramp rate changes occur during load transients, not steady-state production).

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Run turbine at 50% load for 48 hours, then reduce load to 40% using standard ramp rate and measure pressure pulsation; repeat with intervention ramp rate. Instruments: Existing draft-tube pressure sensors (permitted constraint). Pass/fail: Pulsation amplitude reduction ≥30% in intervention run (p < 0.05, t-test). Duration: 96 hours total (2 runs). Kill criterion: If pulsation increases in intervention run, mechanism fails.
